in_text_mentions: May-Thurner syndrome (MTS), coined after Dr. May R. and Dr. Thurner J., is a condition describing the phenomenon of sinistral occurrence of thrombosis of the pelvic veins due to extrinsic venous outflow obstruction. It has been defined as the compression of the left iliofemoral vein by the right common iliac artery against the vertebral body (Figure 1) [1]. It is a rare cause of extensive DVT, compared to the usual presentation of DVTs that are more commonly seen as a result of various underlying illnesses.
